chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant. She gave birth before four months and ten days had passed, then she married. So he ruled that he should separate from her, then not propose to her until the later of the two terms has expired. Then if the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her to him, and if they wish, they may withhold her. If they withhold her, they must return his wealth to him.

key_terms.آخِرُ الْأَجَلَيْنِ: the later of the two waiting terms
key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَ عَشَرَةُ أَيَّامٍ: the standard waiting period of a widow
key_terms.مَالَهُ: his financial payment or property given in the marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pregnant widow gives birth before four months and ten days and remarries before completing her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pregnant widow who gave birth before the completion of four months and ten days and then remarried. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled that the marriage be suspended until the longer waiting period is completed, and that the woman's guardians then retain authority either to remarry her to the same man or decline and return his payment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4791 - Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"The Commander of the Faithful (as) passed judgment regarding a woman whose husband had passed away while she was pregnant. She gave birth before the completion of four months and ten days, and then she married another man.
Imam (as) ruled that she must be separated from him and that he should not propose to her again until the longer of the two waiting periods is completed. If the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her to him, and if they wish, they may prevent it. If they prevent it, they must return his wealth to him."
